evidence: src/infrastructure/ProjectController.ts, TaskController.ts and UserController.ts all import `asString` and `bodyOf` from './requestValues' and use them for every body and query field, so input parsing is handled the same way everywhere.

src/infrastructure/errorHandler.ts: `STATUS_BY_CODE: Record<DomainErrorCode, number>` is the only place that maps domain errors to HTTP statuses; the controllers only set the success statuses 201 and 200.

src/infrastructure/compositionRoot.ts: `buildUseCases()` is the only place that creates the InMemory*Repository classes and UuidGenerator; app.ts (`createApp(useCases: UseCases)`) receives the use cases already built.
src/infrastructure/TaskController.ts: `create`, `list`, `assign` and `done` each call a single use case's `execute` and never call a repository directly.
src/infrastructure/InMemoryTaskRepository.ts: `findByProject(projectId, filter: TaskFilter)` implements the domain repository's query contract, so it does not duplicate a domain rule.
src/infrastructure/server.ts only connects `createApp(buildUseCases())` to `listen`, which keeps process startup separate from route mapping and wiring.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This module is the project's infrastructure adapter layer, and every file plays one part in that job: persistence adapters (the three InMemory*Repository classes), an ID adapter (UuidGenerator), HTTP adapters (the three controllers, errorHandler and requestValues), and wiring (compositionRoot, app, server). In a three-layer model, holding persistence, HTTP and wiring adapters together in infrastructure is the intended boundary, not a split into unrelated concerns.

The module uses its own abstractions consistently. All three controllers parse request input through the shared helpers asString and bodyOf in requestValues.ts, and none of them re-implements that parsing inline. Each controller calls an application use case and never touches a repository directly. Domain errors are turned into HTTP statuses in one place only (STATUS_BY_CODE in errorHandler.ts), and no controller sets error statuses itself. Wiring also lives in one place: buildUseCases builds the dependency graph, createApp maps routes, and server.ts only starts the server.

The three repositories repeat the same Map-based save/findById code, but that is simple boilerplate, not a duplicated business rule or invariant. The status and assignee filtering in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject implements the TaskFilter query contract from the domain; it is not a copy of a domain rule. I found no bypasses or duplicated invariants.
